dossier.purpose: ast-grep (Rust; binary `ast-grep`, deprecated alias `sg`) parses source with tree-sitter and provides syntax-tree search (`run -p/-k`), YAML-rule linting with fixes (`scan`), rule tests (`test`), scaffolding (`new`) and pattern-based rewriting (`run -r`, written to disk only in an `-i` or `-U` session), plus Node.js, Python and WASM bindings (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:51-70; crates/cli/src/utils/args.rs:118-128). Two subcommands bear on code navigation: `outline` (added in 0.44.0, CHANGELOG.md:154) prints a syntactic index of top-level items, members, imports and exports with byte and line/column ranges and a signature line, from 14 bundled YAML rule files covering 15 languages (crates/outline/src/model.rs:87-118; crates/outline/src/default_rule.rs:7-35); `lsp` runs a stdio language server that publishes diagnostics, quick-fix/fix-all code actions and rule-note hovers computed only from the project's ast-grep YAML rules (crates/lsp/src/lib.rs:91-101). It is a syntax-level tool: the code has no definition/reference resolution, rename, LSP-client or MCP functionality (crates/outline/src/model.rs:5-7; no such handlers in crates/lsp), and no Claude Code or Codex integration exists in this repository. Findings come from static reading of the 0.45.3 tree (nothing was built or run); the documentation site (ast-grep.github.io) is outside the repo and was not read. Revision checked via .git/packed-refs:2 and .git/HEAD:1.

claims.claim: ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting.

It is an abstract-syntax-tree based tool that searches code by pattern, 'matching AST nodes instead of text'; patterns are written like ordinary code and match code with the same syntactical structure.
A dollar sign plus upper-case letters (for example $MATCH) is a wildcard that matches any single AST node.
The core is an algorithm to search and replace code based on the abstract syntax tree produced by tree-sitter; it supports lightweight static analysis and massive-scale code manipulation.
jQuery like API for AST traversal and manipulation.
YAML configuration to write new linting rules or code modification.
Written in a compiled language, with tree-sitter based parsing and utilizing multiple cores.
Installable from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise or MacPorts.

Further documented methods: scoop (`scoop install main/ast-grep`), MacPorts (`sudo port install ast-grep`), `nix-shell -p ast-grep`, `mise use -g ast-grep`; for npm, 'pnpm approve-builds may be needed'.
Build from source with rustup and `cargo install --path ./crates/cli --locked`.
CLI form: `ast-grep --pattern 'var code = $PATTERN' --rewrite 'let code = new $PATTERN' --lang ts`; the examples also use -p, -l, -r and -i (interactive).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, update check or phone-home found, and no account, API key or hosted service is required. Evidence: (1) no HTTP/TLS/telemetry crate among the 282 packages in Cargo.lock (searched reqwest, hyper, ureq, curl, rustls, openssl, native-tls, h2, tungstenite, socket2, sentry, posthog, opentelemetry; only `mio` appears, via crossterm and signal-hook-mio, and tokio's lock entry has no mio or socket2 dependency: Cargo.lock:1911-1919); (2) a search of crates/ for telemetry, analytics, reqwest, hyper, ureq, curl, TcpStream, UdpSocket, std::net and tokio::net returned nothing; (3) every locked dependency comes from crates.io or workspace paths, with no git sources (Cargo.lock); (4) runtime I/O is local: files, stdin/stdout (the LSP server speaks stdio, crates/cli/src/lsp.rs:18-19), and the only subprocesses are $EDITOR for interactive edits (crates/cli/src/print/interactive_print.rs:391-392) and the `sg` forwarder (crates/cli/src/bin/alias.rs:25). Network is needed only to install (npm, PyPI, crates.io, and GitHub Releases for cargo-binstall: crates/cli/Cargo.toml:62-67). Related local-execution surface: customLanguages in sgconfig.yml loads native shared libraries at startup (crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs:120-142).

code.architecture: Cargo workspace of 10 crates plus xtask (Cargo.toml:1-7). crates/core (ast-grep-core): tree-sitter-backed document/node model (tree_sitter/mod.rs: StrDoc and a per-thread Parser cache), pattern compiler and matcher (matcher/pattern.rs, match_tree/), metavariables (meta_var.rs), replacers and templates (replacer/). crates/config (ast-grep-config): YAML rule model and engine (rule_config.rs, rule_core.rs, rule/ atomic, relational and composite rules, transform/, fixer.rs, combined.rs CombinedScan, rule_collection.rs). crates/language: SupportLang enum of 28 built-in languages, each behind an optional tree-sitter grammar crate in the default builtin-parser feature (lib.rs:259-288; Cargo.toml:48-84). crates/dynamic: custom tree-sitter grammars loaded as shared libraries via libloading (lib.rs:120-142). crates/outline: outline model (model.rs), YAML-driven extractors (extractor.rs, combined_extractor.rs, options.rs) and 14 bundled rule files (default_rules/*.yml, include_str! in default_rule.rs). crates/lsp: tower-lsp-server Backend converting rule matches into diagnostics, code actions and hovers (lib.rs, utils.rs). crates/cli: clap front end (lib.rs dispatch; run.rs, scan.rs, verify.rs, new.rs, outline.rs and outline/, lsp.rs, completions.rs), sgconfig.yml discovery and project config (config.rs), SgLang = built-in plus custom languages, globs and injections (lang/), printers (print/: colored, JSON, interactive, GitHub/SARIF, file names) and a producer-threads / single-consumer pipeline over the ignore crate's parallel walker (utils/worker.rs:12-56,118-150). crates/napi, crates/pyo3, crates/wasm: Node, Python and WASM bindings (publish = false; shipped through npm and PyPI). xtask: JSON schema generation (schemas/*.json) and release bumping. Runtime flow: parse args, discover sgconfig.yml upward from the current directory (registers custom languages, globs and injections), walk files in parallel, tree-sitter parse, pattern or rule match, then print or rewrite in place on accept or --update-all (crates/cli/src/print/interactive_print.rs:55-66).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: (a) GitHub Release zips named app-<target>.zip containing `ast-grep` and `sg` for 7 targets - Windows x86_64/i686/aarch64 (MSVC), macOS aarch64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/aarch64 glibc (.github/workflows/release.yml:35-70); (b) crates.io publish of the workspace crates on tag via katyo/publish-crates (release.yml:13-22); (c) npm `@ast-grep/cli` plus 7 platform packages published with `npm publish` using an NPM_TOKEN written to ~/.npmrc, with binaries re-downloaded from the latest GitHub release rather than passed from the build job (release.yml:71-116); (d) PyPI `ast-grep-cli` wheels (macOS x86_64 and universal2, Windows x64/x86/arm64, Linux manylinux_2_28 x86_64/aarch64) plus sdist, uploaded with `uv publish` in a job granted an OIDC id-token for trusted publishing (.github/workflows/pypi.yml:28-190); (e) PyPI `ast-grep-py` wheels for Python 3.10-3.14, uploaded with maturin-action and id-token (.github/workflows/pyo3.yml:32-167); (f) npm `@ast-grep/napi` built for 9 targets including musl and linux arm64 (.github/workflows/napi.yml:19-162) and `@ast-grep/wasm` (.github/workflows/wasm.yml:21-112). claim_checks.claim: ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting (README.md:19).
claim_checks.evidence: Subcommands run (search/rewrite via -p/-k and -r), scan (YAML-rule lint with fixes), test (rule tests), new, lsp, outline, completions (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:51-70). Rewrites reach disk only in an interactive or --update-all session (crates/cli/src/utils/args.rs:118-128; crates/cli/src/print/interactive_print.rs:55-66).

claim_checks.claim: The tool is named 'ast-grep(sg)' and `sg` is the short command (README.md:17,19).
claim_checks.evidence: The `sg` binary still ships but has been deprecated since 0.45.0: it prints 'WARNING: `sg` is deprecated. Use `ast-grep` instead.' on every run (crates/cli/src/bin/alias.rs:1-8,22-24), a test asserts the warning (crates/cli/tests/help_test.rs:8-24) and CHANGELOG.md:71 records the deprecation. The README does not mention it, so the code is ahead of the README.

claim_checks.claim: A dollar sign plus upper-case letters (e.g. $MATCH) matches any single AST node (README.md:24).
claim_checks.evidence: Names may also contain digits and underscore; $_ is an unnamed drop, $$$ and $$$A match multiple nodes, and $$A is a distinct form (crates/core/src/meta_var.rs:223-281). A single-dollar capture matches only named tree-sitter nodes; unnamed tokens need the double-dollar form (crates/core/src/match_tree/mod.rs:61-82), so 'any single AST node' is a simplification.

claim_checks.claim: The core algorithm searches and replaces code on the AST produced by tree-sitter (README.md:103).
claim_checks.evidence: crates/core/src/tree_sitter/mod.rs:62-112 (StrDoc wraps a tree_sitter::Tree parsed through a per-thread Parser cache, lines 33-60); replacement is exercised in crates/core/src/lib.rs:43-49 (replace 'var $A = $B' with 'let $A = $B').

claim_checks.claim: jQuery like API for AST traversal and manipulation (README.md:111).
claim_checks.evidence: Present in the library bindings only, not in the CLI: Node SgNode has find/findAll, parent/children/next/prev/ancestors/field, matches/inside/has/precedes/follows and replace/commitEdits (crates/napi/src/sg_node.rs:122-379); the Python stubs list the same (crates/pyo3/ast_grep_py/ast_grep_py.pyi:34-70); the WASM README documents it (crates/wasm/README.md:140-206).

claim_checks.claim: YAML configuration to write new linting rules or code modification (README.md:113).
claim_checks.evidence: Rules are deserialized from YAML with an optional fix (crates/config/src/lib.rs:34-49; example YAML with fix parsed in crates/lsp/tests/basic.rs:74-87; crates/lsp/src/utils.rs:33-37 consumes rule.fixer). `scan` loads rules from sgconfig.yml ruleDirs, --rule or --inline-rules (crates/cli/src/scan.rs:31-43,149-164; crates/cli/src/config.rs:184-241).

claim_checks.claim: Written in a compiled language with tree-sitter parsing, utilizing multiple cores (README.md:115).
claim_checks.evidence: Rust 2024 workspace (Cargo.toml:15-16). Files are walked in parallel with the ignore crate and processed by producer threads feeding a single printer thread (crates/cli/src/utils/args.rs:56-74,98-100; crates/cli/src/utils/worker.rs:12-56,118-150); the automatic thread count is capped at 12 (args.rs:66-74). No benchmark in the tree substantiates speed; the changelog says benchmarks were moved out of the repo (CHANGELOG.md:129).

claim_checks.claim: Install from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise or MacPorts (README.md:34).
claim_checks.evidence: Repo-backed channels: npm @ast-grep/cli (npm/package.json:2,29-44), PyPI ast-grep-cli (pyproject.toml:6; .github/workflows/pypi.yml), crates.io `ast-grep` (crates/cli/Cargo.toml:2; release.yml:13-22) and cargo-binstall metadata pointing at the release zips (crates/cli/Cargo.toml:62-67; release.yml:56-65). risks: Scope gap for the stated navigation needs: ast-grep is a syntax-level (tree-sitter) tool. The repo has no MCP server or client and no Claude Code/Codex integration (case-insensitive searches for mcp, model context protocol, claude, codex and anthropic found nothing). `ast-grep lsp` advertises only full-text sync, code actions, one executeCommand and hover (crates/lsp/src/lib.rs:91-101) and has no definition, references, rename or symbol handlers (none in crates/lsp). Nothing launches or talks to other language servers; the only subprocesses are $EDITOR and the `sg` forwarder (crates/cli/src/print/interactive_print.rs:391-392; crates/cli/src/bin/alias.rs:25). The outline model states it does not build a semantic graph of references (crates/outline/src/model.rs:5-7), and no scope or type resolution code was found.

The bundled language server is rule-driven and project-bound: `ast-grep lsp` fails with the missing-project error (exit code 3) unless a valid sgconfig.yml is found (crates/cli/src/lsp.rs:17; crates/cli/src/utils/error_context.rs:83,279-283); diagnostics come only from the project's YAML rules (crates/lsp/src/lib.rs:276-313); only file:// URIs are handled (lib.rs:585-589); documents outside the first workspace folder or cwd are skipped (lib.rs:370-386); sync is full-document with a TODO for incremental (lib.rs:92-93) and every change re-parses the whole document (lib.rs:445-473). The CLI-level startup test is ignored (crates/cli/src/lsp.rs:47-52), although crates/lsp/tests/basic.rs has 11 tests.

The structural index (`outline`) is new and partial: added in 0.44.0 on 2026-06-21 (CHANGELOG.md:125-127,154) and still changing in 0.45.x (CHANGELOG.md:11-12,36); bundled extractor rules cover 15 of the 28 built-in languages (crates/outline/src/default_rules/*.yml versus crates/language/src/lib.rs:259-288), with none for Bash, CSS, Dart, Elixir, Haskell, HCL, HTML, JSON, Lua, Nix, Scala, Solidity or YAML. Entries carry name, kind, ranges and a template-derived or first-source-line signature, not the definition body (crates/outline/src/model.rs:87-118; crates/outline/src/extractor.rs:68-70), so exact source needs a second read by range. The outline JSON has no schema-version field (crates/cli/src/outline/extract.rs:30-36).

Native-code loading from project config: `customLanguages` in sgconfig.yml makes ast-grep load the named shared library and call its symbol at startup (crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs:120-142; crates/dynamic/src/custom_lang.rs:37-63). Config discovery walks from the current directory up to the filesystem root (crates/cli/src/config.rs:280-299) and runs before argument parsing, so any invocation, even --help, inside a tree containing such a file loads it (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:131-140; crates/cli/src/config.rs:98-114). Running ast-grep in an untrusted checkout can therefore execute code chosen by that checkout's config. The repo also ships prebuilt .so fixtures used by tests (fixtures/json-linux.so, fixtures/json-mac.so; crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs:284-291). There are 54 `unsafe` matches in 15 Rust files (largest: crates/wasm/src/sg_node.rs, crates/core/src/pinned.rs, crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs) and no forbid(unsafe_code).

Release and supply-chain controls are thin: no SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting policy; no checksum, signature, SBOM or provenance step in any workflow; workflow actions are referenced by mutable tags or branches, none by commit SHA; npm publishes use a long-lived NPM_TOKEN with plain `npm publish` and no --provenance (.github/workflows/release.yml:103-116), and the CLI npm packages are built from zips re-downloaded from the latest GitHub release (release.yml:80-85); Renovate automerges patch/pin/digest updates (renovate.json:6-10); no cargo-audit or cargo-deny job or config was found.

Pre-1.0 and fast-moving: five releases dated 2026-06-21 to 2026-08-23 (CHANGELOG.md:22,46,69,99,127); 0.44.0 lists three 'Breaking change' entries in library crates (CHANGELOG.md:164,166,169); the `sg` command was deprecated in 0.45.0 (CHANGELOG.md:71; crates/cli/src/bin/alias.rs:1-8); PyPI classifiers still say 'Development Status :: 3 - Alpha' (pyproject.toml:21). Manifests name a single author (Cargo.toml:14) and the README asks for sponsorship to free maintainer time (README.md:95-99). The 0.45.3 entry carries no release date (CHANGELOG.md:7-18). No search or outline performance benchmarks are published in this tree; the changelog says benchmarks were moved out of the repo (CHANGELOG.md:129).

Platform and CI gaps: no musl Linux CLI artifact (release zips are glibc only, release.yml:49-52) and the npm CLI launcher finds no package on musl and exits 1 (npm/postinstall.js:16,64-67), although the NAPI binding builds musl targets (napi.yml:39-41,50-52); WSL2 is not mentioned anywhere; on Unix `sg` only forwards to an `ast-grep` found on PATH (crates/cli/src/bin/alias.rs:19-33); pull requests run only the ubuntu-latest jobs in coverage.yaml (lines 6,12,32,53), while macOS/Windows and binding builds run on tags, manual dispatch or the daily cron (napi.yml:6-13, pyo3.yml:15-26, pypi.yml:3-14, wasm.yml:7-19); CI uses stable Rust and no job exercises the declared MSRV 1.88.0 (Cargo.toml:20; coverage.yaml:19).

Dependency notes: serde_yaml, used for all rule and config YAML parsing in crates/config, crates/cli and crates/outline, is locked at 0.9.34+deprecated (Cargo.lock:1639-1640; Cargo.toml:36); the LSP stack is pre-1.0 (tower-lsp-server 0.23.0 and ls-types 0.0.6: Cargo.lock:1009-1010,2015-2016); tree-sitter is 0.27.0 with 27 separately versioned grammar crates, one consumed through the renamed fork crate tree-sitter-kotlin-sg (crates/language/Cargo.toml:20-46; Cargo.lock:2255-2256). The project itself is MIT (LICENSE); licenses of transitive crates were not audited here and no deny.toml exists.
